name: AuthSignIn
title: Blocks/Auth/AuthSignIn
summary: The signed-out screens of a platform app, frame included: a full-height page with the signed-out `AppHeader` (the product mark and a Documentation button) over a centred column that holds one `Card` and the prompt and terms under it. It serves /login, /signup and /signup/verify, and the signed-in hand-offs that share the frame: the OAuth authorize screen (scopes, Allow / Deny) and device or CLI authorization (compare the code, Confirm). An app that signs in with an Azion personal token instead of an account uses the PersonalToken variant (`token-sign-in.vue`): one masked `PasswordInput` for the token, a link to where tokens are created, a Remember for this tab option, and a `sign-in` event that hands the token to the app, which answers with `loading` and `error`. The Google and GitHub buttons lead the card, over an “or” `Separator`. The card opens on a `PageHeader` and signs in in two steps: email, then password. Each field is a `Field` whose `Field.Label` sits over an `Input`, or over a `PasswordInput` with `PasswordRequirements`; a `FieldError` (email) or `Field.Error` (password) appears only after the primary action. While a request is in flight the primary `Button` shows its loading state and the step's fieldset is disabled. The rest is `Button`, `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`, a `Tag` and an `Alert`. Errors follow one rule: auth never toasts. Each error story is the primary flow with one endpoint response: the same two-step card on its password step, and the outcome in the same small `Alert` under the heading. What changes is the severity and what it carries: nothing after a 401, because the fields under it are the recovery; Retry when nobody can fix it (503, 500, timeout); the Sign in and reset-your-password links when the address is already registered (409). In-page actions (Forgot your password?, Resend email, Set a new password) are `Button` with `variant="link"`, never an anchor to `#`. Built from `PageHeader`, `AppHeader`, `Tag`, `Card`, `Alert`, `Input`, `Field`, `PasswordInput`, `PasswordRequirements`, `FieldError` and `Button`. The card column slides in from the inline start with a fade on mount (`starting:` styles, `duration-slow-01`, `ease-expressive-entrance`, none under reduced motion), and the card height eases between steps. A full page routed outside ConsoleLayout.

variants.name: SignUp
variants.summary: The sign-up screen: create an account with a work email, Google or GitHub.

variants.name: SessionExpired
variants.summary: The /login screen after a session expires: it opens on the password step for the same email, with an info Alert that clears on the next action.

variants.name: ProvidersLoading
variants.summary: The /login screen while the identity providers load: two `Skeleton` bars in a `role="status"` region named Preparing sign-in providers take the place of the Google and GitHub buttons; email sign-in works meanwhile.

variants.name: Submitting
variants.summary: Sign in in flight: the password step with the primary Button loading, the fieldset disabled and the form marked busy until the request answers.

variants.name: CheckInbox
variants.summary: The /signup/verify screen: where the verification link went, the resend prompt, and a secondary Return to sign in action.

variants.name: IncorrectCredentials
variants.summary: 401 on Sign in, on the password step of the same two-step card: a danger message under the heading with no action, and the password cleared.

variants.name: ServiceUnavailable
variants.summary: 503 on Sign in, on the password step: a warning message that keeps the credentials and carries Retry, the only move left.

variants.name: ServerError
variants.summary: 500 on Sign in, on the password step: tied to no field, so where the console would toast, the card keeps a danger message with Retry.

variants.name: Timeout
variants.summary: No response to Sign in, on the password step: the same message as the 500 but warning, because the request may still have gone through, with Retry.

variants.name: EmailAlreadyRegistered
variants.summary: 409 on Sign up: a danger message carrying the two ways out as links, Sign in or reset your password, with the address left in the field.

variants.name: MfaSetup
variants.summary: Turn on multi-factor authentication: steps, the QR code with a copyable setup key, and a 6-digit OtpInput that verifies on complete; wrong code on the field, no answer as a warning with Retry.

variants.name: MfaCode
variants.summary: The sign-in MFA challenge: a 6-digit OtpInput, focused when the challenge opens, that submits when full, a recovery-code mode (8 characters, grouped), and Sign in with another account.

variants.name: OauthConsent
variants.summary: The OAuth authorize screen: the requesting app with its publisher and site, the signed-in account with Switch account, the scopes it asks for as a list, where Allow sends you, and Deny / Allow, each settling in the card's notice.

variants.name: DeviceAuthorization
variants.summary: Device or CLI authorization: the code the terminal printed, shown large to compare, the request details (application, device, IP address, time), the account and scopes, Cancel / Confirm, and a typed code entry (8 characters, grouped by 4) when the codes do not match.

variants.name: PersonalToken
variants.summary: Sign in with an Azion personal token, for an app with no accounts of its own. The card is `token-sign-in.vue`, driven by props: one masked, monospace `PasswordInput` with show and hide, a link to how tokens are created, required and no-spaces checks on the field, a Remember for this tab `Checkbox` (`v-model:remember`, off by default; the block stores nothing), and a `sign-in` event `(event, token)`. The app checks the token and answers with `loading`, then `error` (`rejected`, `no-access`, `rate-limited`, `unreachable` or a message).

variants.name: RejectedToken
variants.summary: `error="rejected"` (a 401 on the personal token): the same card with the danger notice under the heading, the field cleared and focused for another paste.

variants.name: NoAccessToken
variants.summary: `error="no-access"` (a 403: the token is valid but lacks the permissions the app reads): a danger notice that says to create a token with access, the field cleared and focused.
